question: A policy officer has one hour before a board meeting and a Claude-written briefing containing roughly twenty factual claims. She cannot check them all. What should she do first?
options: A) Ask Claude which of the claims in the briefing are the ones most likely to be incorrect.
B) Check the claims that are easiest to look up, so that the largest number get covered.
C) Work through the claims in the order they appear until the hour she has available runs out.
D) Identify the few claims the board's decision actually rests on and verify those ones first.
correct_answers: D) Identify the few claims the board's decision actually rests on and verify those ones first.
explanations: Incorrect. Claude has no independent view of which of its own statements are unsupported, so this ranking is generated the same way the claims were.
Incorrect. Maximising the count optimises for the wrong thing; easy claims are often the low-stakes ones.
Incorrect. Order of appearance has no relationship to importance, so the claims that matter most may sit in the part she never reaches.
Correct. When verification time is scarce it has to be spent where an error would change the decision, so triage by consequence comes before any checking begins.
